items.text:
वृकश्वानसृगालाद्यैर्दष्टो यस्तु द्विजोत्तमः ।
स्नात्वा जपेत्स गायत्रीं पवित्रां वेदमातरं ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
vṛkaśvānasṛgālādyairdaṣṭo yastu dvijottamaḥ |
snātvā japetsa gāyatrīṃ pavitrāṃ vedamātaraṃ || 1 ||
items.en: If a good twice-born man is bitten by a wolf, a dog, a jackal or a similar animal, he should bathe and then recite the Gāyatrī, the pure mother of the Vedas.
items.note: Gāyatrī: the most sacred Vedic verse (Ṛgveda 3.62.10), recited daily by twice-born men.

items.text:
गवां शृङ्गोदकैः स्नानं महानद्योस्तु संगमे ।
समुद्रदर्शनाद्वापि शुना दष्टः शुचिर्भवेत् ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
gavāṃ śṛṅgodakaiḥ snānaṃ mahānadyostu saṃgame |
samudradarśanādvāpi śunā daṣṭaḥ śucirbhavet || 2 ||
items.en: A person bitten by a dog becomes pure by bathing in water poured over cows' horns, or by bathing where two great rivers meet, or even just by seeing the ocean.

items.text:
वेदविद्याव्रतस्नातः शुना दष्टो द्विजो यदि ।
स हिरण्योदकैः स्नात्वा घृतं प्राश्य विशुध्यति ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
vedavidyāvratasnātaḥ śunā daṣṭo dvijo yadi |
sa hiraṇyodakaiḥ snātvā ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati || 3 ||
items.en: If a twice-born man who has finished his Vedic study and vows is bitten by a dog, he becomes pure by bathing in water that has touched gold and then eating ghee.

items.text:
सव्रतस्तु शुना दष्टो यस्त्रिरात्रं उपावसेत् ।
घृतं कुशोदकं पीत्वा व्रतशेषं समापयेत् ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
savratastu śunā daṣṭo yastrirātraṃ upāvaset |
ghṛtaṃ kuśodakaṃ pītvā vrataśeṣaṃ samāpayet || 4 ||
items.en: One who is in the middle of a religious vow and is bitten by a dog should fast for three nights. Then, after drinking ghee and water with kuśa grass in it, he should finish the rest of his vow.
items.note: kuśa: a sacred grass used in Vedic rites.

items.text:
अव्रतः सव्रतो वापि शुना दष्टो भवेद्द्विजः ।
प्रणिपत्य भवेत्पूतो विप्रैश्चक्षुर्निरीक्षितः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
avrataḥ savrato vāpi śunā daṣṭo bhaveddvijaḥ |
praṇipatya bhavetpūto vipraiścakṣurnirīkṣitaḥ || 5 ||
items.en: Whether he is under a vow or not, a twice-born man bitten by a dog becomes pure by bowing down to Brahmins and being looked at by them.

items.text:
शुना घ्रातावलीढस्य नखैर्विलिखितस्य च ।
अद्भिः प्रक्षालनं प्रोक्तं अग्निना चोपचूलनम् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
śunā ghrātāvalīḍhasya nakhairvilikhitasya ca |
adbhiḥ prakṣālanaṃ proktaṃ agninā copacūlanam || 6 ||
items.en: If a dog has sniffed or licked someone, or scratched him with its claws, the rule is to wash the place with water and to warm it with fire.
items.note: Upacūlana is read here as warming or lightly singeing the spot with fire.

items.text:
शुना तु ब्राह्मणी दष्टा जम्बुकेन वृकेण वा ।
उदितं ग्रहनक्षत्रं दृष्ट्वा सद्यः शुचिर्भवेत् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
śunā tu brāhmaṇī daṣṭā jambukena vṛkeṇa vā |
uditaṃ grahanakṣatraṃ dṛṣṭvā sadyaḥ śucirbhavet || 7 ||
items.en: A Brahmin woman bitten by a dog, a jackal or a wolf becomes pure at once by looking at the planets and stars when they rise.

items.text:
कृष्णपक्षे यदा सोमो न दृश्येत कदाचन ।
यां दिशं व्रजते सोमस्तां दिशं वावलोकयेत् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
kṛṣṇapakṣe yadā somo na dṛśyeta kadācana |
yāṃ diśaṃ vrajate somastāṃ diśaṃ vāvalokayet || 8 ||
items.en: In the dark half of the month, when the moon cannot be seen at all, she should look in the direction in which the moon is moving.

items.text:
असद्ब्राह्मणके ग्रामे शुना दष्टो द्विजोत्तमः ।
वृषं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य सद्यः स्नात्वा शुचिर्भवेत् ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
asadbrāhmaṇake grāme śunā daṣṭo dvijottamaḥ |
vṛṣaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sadyaḥ snātvā śucirbhavet || 9 ||
items.en: If a good twice-born man is bitten by a dog in a village that has no proper Brahmins, he becomes pure at once by walking around a bull with his right side towards it and then bathing.

items.text:
चण्डालेन श्वपाकेन गोभिर्विप्रैर्हतो यदि ।
आहिताग्निर्मृतो विप्रो विषेणात्महतो यदि ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
caṇḍālena śvapākena gobhirviprairhato yadi |
āhitāgnirmṛto vipro viṣeṇātmahato yadi || 10 ||
items.en: Suppose a Brahmin who keeps the sacred fires is killed by a Caṇḍāla, a Śvapāka, cows or Brahmins, or kills himself with poison.
items.note: āhitāgni: a man who has formally set up and keeps the household sacred fires. Caṇḍāla and Śvapāka ('dog-cooker'): groups treated as the lowest, outside the four varṇas.

items.text:
दहेत्तं ब्राह्मणं विप्रो लोकाग्नौ मन्त्रवर्जितम् ।
स्पृष्ट्वा वोढ्वा च दग्ध्वा च सपिण्डेषु च सर्वथा ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
dahettaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vipro lokāgnau mantravarjitam |
spṛṣṭvā voḍhvā ca dagdhvā ca sapiṇḍeṣu ca sarvathā || 11 ||
items.en: Then a Brahmin should burn that Brahmin's body in an ordinary fire, without mantras. Anyone who touched, carried or burnt the body, and in every case his sapiṇḍa relatives,
items.note: sapiṇḍa: close relatives who share offerings to the same ancestors. The sentence continues in the next verse.

items.text:
प्राजापत्यं चरेत्पश्चाद्विप्राणां अनुशासनात् ।
दग्धास्थीनि पुनर्गृह्य क्षीरैः प्रक्षालयेद्द्विजः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
prājāpatyaṃ caretpaścādviprāṇāṃ anuśāsanāt |
dagdhāsthīni punargṛhya kṣīraiḥ prakṣālayeddvijaḥ || 12 ||
items.en: … should afterwards perform the Prājāpatya penance as the Brahmins direct. Then the twice-born should collect the burnt bones again and wash them with milk,
items.note: Prājāpatya: a 12-day penance (3 days one meal by day, 3 days one meal at night, 3 days only food given unasked, 3 days full fast).

items.text:
पुनर्दहेत्स्वाग्निना तु स्वतन्त्रेण पृथक्पृथक् ।
आहिताग्निर्द्विजः कश्चित्प्रवसन्कालचोदितः ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
punardahetsvāgninā tu svatantreṇa pṛthakpṛthak |
āhitāgnirdvijaḥ kaścitpravasankālacoditaḥ || 13 ||
items.en: … and burn them again, separately, in the dead man's own sacred fire with its proper rite. Now, if a twice-born man who keeps the sacred fires is travelling away from home and his time comes,

items.text:
देहनाशं अनुप्राप्तस्तस्याग्निर्वसते गृहे ।
प्रेताग्निहोत्रसंस्कारः श्रूयतां ऋषिपुङ्गवाः ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
dehanāśaṃ anuprāptastasyāgnirvasate gṛhe |
pretāgnihotrasaṃskāraḥ śrūyatāṃ ṛṣipuṅgavāḥ || 14 ||
items.en: … so that he dies while his fire remains at home, then listen, best of sages, to the funeral rite of the agnihotra for such a dead man.
items.note: agnihotra: the daily fire offering made by a man who keeps the sacred fires.

items.text:
कृष्णाजिनं समास्तीर्य कुशैस्तु पुरुषाकृतिम् ।
षट्शतानि शतं चैव पलाशानां च वृन्ततः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
kṛṣṇājinaṃ samāstīrya kuśaistu puruṣākṛtim |
ṣaṭśatāni śataṃ caiva palāśānāṃ ca vṛntataḥ || 15 ||
items.en: One should spread out a black antelope skin and on it make a human figure out of kuśa grass, using seven hundred palāśa leaf-stalks.
items.note: palāśa: the flame-of-the-forest tree (Butea monosperma), sacred in Vedic rites.

items.text:
चत्वारिंशच्छिरे दद्याच्छतं कण्ठे तु विन्यसेत् ।
बाहुभ्यां शतकं दद्यादङ्गुलीषु दशैव तु ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
catvāriṃśacchire dadyācchataṃ kaṇṭhe tu vinyaset |
bāhubhyāṃ śatakaṃ dadyādaṅgulīṣu daśaiva tu || 16 ||
items.en: Place forty stalks for the head and a hundred for the neck. Give a hundred to the arms and ten to the fingers.

items.text:
शतं तु जघने दद्याद्द्विशतं तूदरे तथा ।
दद्यादष्टौ वृषणयोः पञ्च मेध्रे तु विन्यसेत् ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
śataṃ tu jaghane dadyāddviśataṃ tūdare tathā |
dadyādaṣṭau vṛṣaṇayoḥ pañca medhre tu vinyaset || 17 ||
items.en: Put a hundred for the hips and two hundred for the belly. Put eight for the testicles and five for the penis.

items.text:
एकविंशतिं ऊरुभ्यां द्विशतं जानुजङ्घयोः ।
पादाङ्गुलीषु षड्दद्याद्यज्ञपात्रं ततो न्यसेत् ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
ekaviṃśatiṃ ūrubhyāṃ dviśataṃ jānujaṅghayoḥ |
pādāṅgulīṣu ṣaḍdadyādyajñapātraṃ tato nyaset || 18 ||
items.en: Put twenty-one for the thighs, two hundred for the knees and shins, and six for the toes. Then place the sacrificial vessels on the figure.
items.note: The parts listed in 5.16–5.18 add up to 790, not the 700 stated in 5.15; the numbers may be corrupt.

items.text:
शम्यं शिश्ने विनिःक्षिप्य अरणीं मुष्कयोरपि ।
जुहूं च दक्षिणे हस्ते वामे तूपभृतं न्यसेत् ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
śamyaṃ śiśne viniḥkṣipya araṇīṃ muṣkayorapi |
juhūṃ ca dakṣiṇe haste vāme tūpabhṛtaṃ nyaset || 19 ||
items.en: Put the śamyā (yoke-pin) on the penis and the araṇi fire-sticks on the testicles. Put the juhū ladle in the right hand and the upabhṛt ladle in the left.
items.note: araṇi: two wooden sticks rubbed to make sacred fire. juhū and upabhṛt: wooden ladles used to pour offerings.

items.text:
कर्णे चोलूखलं दद्यात्पृष्ठे च मुसलं न्यसेत् ।
उरसि क्षिप्य दृषदं तण्डुलाज्यतिलान्मुखे ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
karṇe colūkhalaṃ dadyātpṛṣṭhe ca musalaṃ nyaset |
urasi kṣipya dṛṣadaṃ taṇḍulājyatilānmukhe || 20 ||
items.en: Put the mortar by the ear and the pestle on the back. Place the grinding stone on the chest, and rice, ghee and sesame in the mouth.
items.note: 'By the ear' (karṇe) is odd, since the ears appear again in the next verse; the reading may be faulty.

items.text:
श्रोत्रे च प्रोक्षणीं दद्यादाज्यस्थलीं तु चक्षुषोः ।
कर्णे नेत्रे मुखे घ्राणे हिरण्यशकलं न्यसेत् ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
śrotre ca prokṣaṇīṃ dadyādājyasthalīṃ tu cakṣuṣoḥ |
karṇe netre mukhe ghrāṇe hiraṇyaśakalaṃ nyaset || 21 ||
items.en: Put the prokṣaṇī (sprinkling vessel) at the ears and the ghee pot at the eyes. Place pieces of gold on the ears, eyes, mouth and nose.

items.text:
अग्निहोत्रोपकरणं अशेषं तत्र निक्षिपेत् ।
असौ स्वर्गाय लोकाय स्वाहेत्येकाहुतिं सकृत् ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
agnihotropakaraṇaṃ aśeṣaṃ tatra nikṣipet |
asau svargāya lokāya svāhetyekāhutiṃ sakṛt || 22 ||
items.en: Put all the remaining agnihotra tools there. Then, saying 'To that man, for the heaven world, svāhā', one single offering

items.text:
दद्यात्पुत्रोऽथवा भ्राताप्यन्यो वापि च बान्धवः ।
यथा दहनसंस्कारस्तथा कार्यं विचक्षणैः ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
dadyātputro'thavā bhrātāpyanyo vāpi ca bāndhavaḥ |
yathā dahanasaṃskārastathā kāryaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ || 23 ||
items.en: … should be made by his son, or a brother, or some other relative. Wise people should carry this out in the same way as a normal cremation.

items.text:
ईदृशं तु विधिं कुर्याद्ब्रह्मलोकगतिः स्मृता ।
दहन्ति ये द्विजास्तं तु ते यान्ति परमां गतिं ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
īdṛśaṃ tu vidhiṃ kuryādbrahmalokagatiḥ smṛtā |
dahanti ye dvijāstaṃ tu te yānti paramāṃ gatiṃ || 24 ||
items.en: If this rite is done in this way, the dead man is said to reach the world of Brahmā. The twice-born who cremate him also reach the highest goal.
items.note: Brahmaloka: the heaven of the god Brahmā.

items.text:
अन्यथा कुर्वते कर्म त्वात्मबुद्ध्या प्रचोदिताः ।
भवन्त्यल्पायुषस्ते वै पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
anyathā kurvate karma tvātmabuddhyā pracoditāḥ |
bhavantyalpāyuṣaste vai patanti narake'śucau || 25 ||
items.en: Those who do the rite in some other way, guided only by their own ideas, become short-lived and fall into a filthy hell.
